title: Exchange law for whiskered natural transformations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be categories [def-nagata-category], $F,G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $H,K:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ functors, and $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$, $\theta:H\Rightarrow K$ natural transformations. With composition of functors read from right to left, the two whiskered composites from $HF$ to $KG$ agree:
$$(K\eta)\circ(\theta F)=(\theta G)\circ(H\eta).$$
Here $(K\eta)_x=K(\eta_x)$ and $(\theta F)_x=\theta_{F(x)}$, and similarly for the other two whiskerings. A functor here assigns objects and morphisms preserving identities and composition. A natural transformation $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ is a family $\eta_x:F(x)\to G(x)$ with $G(u)\circ\eta_x=\eta_y\circ F(u)$ for every morphism $u:x\to y$; the same convention applies to $\theta$.
